Expectation1: Attending children's school events and activities
Situation1: The school reports that the child was caught bullying a classmate, and the mother needs to respond
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Story: I was just about to leave for my daughter’s school assembly when the phone rang. It was the principal, her voice tense—my daughter had been caught bullying a classmate. She wanted me to come in immediately to discuss what happened. My heart sank; I knew I had to be there for my child, to understand, to guide her, and to show the school I took this seriously. As I grabbed my keys, my phone buzzed again. It was my best friend, panicked—she was on her way to the airport and thought she’d left her passport at home. She begged me to check and, if it was there, to rush it to her before her flight. I could hear the desperation in her voice; she had been looking forward to this trip for months, and I was the only one she could count on. I stood frozen in my hallway, torn between my daughter’s crisis and my friend’s emergency, feeling the weight of both their needs pressing down on me, unsure which way to turn.
